1. Map entry removal reports the key and value swapped 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>RemoveMapEntryAssignment passes null into the key parameter and the real key term into the
>value parameter of CollectionElementAssignment's constructor, whose signature is `(columnId,
>operator, key, value, opening, closing)`. The rendered CQL is correct only because
>buildRightOperand prints just the non-null value, but getKey() now returns null and
>getValue() returns the map key term, and isIdempotent() is evaluated against that same term.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[query-builder/src/main/java/com/datastax/oss/driver/internal/querybuilder/update/RemoveMapEntryAssignment.java[31]](https://github.com/scylladb/java-driver/pull/1467/files#diff-d8cabc3ee37d5ca8577987103bc3da780d53c0144c8f7bb9de441cb591f59663R31-R31) > >```diff >+ super(columnId, Operator.REMOVE, null, key, '{', '}'); >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >In `RemoveMapEntryAssignment`, the constructor calls `super(columnId, Operator.REMOVE, null, key, '{', '}')`. The `CollectionElementAssignment` constructor takes `(columnId, operator, key, value, opening, closing)`, so the map key is stored in the `value` field and `getKey()` returns null. The text output is right only because the null key is skipped during rendering. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- query-builder/src/main/java/com/datastax/oss/driver/internal/querybuilder/update/RemoveMapEntryAssignment.java[27-33] >- query-builder/src/main/java/com/datastax/oss/driver/internal/querybuilder/update/CollectionElementAssignment.java[51-80] > >## Recommended Fix >Change the super call to pass the key in the key slot and a value that is not rendered. The simplest correct option is to have the subclass pass `key` as the `key` argument and make the rendering path print only the key when the operator is REMOVE with an opening `{` and no value. Alternatively, add a protected constructor or a dedicated `buildRightOperand` override in `RemoveMapEntryAssignment` that renders `{` + key + `}` and stores `key` in the key field, keeping `getKey()` and `getValue()` consistent with the public API. Add a unit test asserting `getKey()` returns the key term. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
